title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Site Ops, and Top Support Issues
author: Priya Shah
content:
Overview

Purpose
- This living document describes the canonical Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation artifacts we maintain: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the top support issues with canonical fixes. It is intended for Docs writers, SDK owners, DevEx engineers, and on-call support.

Scope
- Languages and SDK surface: Python, JavaScript (Node), Go, and Java.
- Quickstarts & templates for common patterns: text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking, streaming responses, and function/tool calling.
- API examples used in public docs and internal troubleshooting playbooks.
- Docs site operating procedures (publishing workflow, review, release cadence).
- Top support issues and canonical fixes that reduce repeated incidents and mean-time-to-resolution.

1) SDK Guides (owner: DevEx SDK team)

Overview
- Each SDK must include: installation, quickstart, auth and config, core APIs (generate/chat/embed), streaming example, error handling, retries/backoff, and a migration guide for breaking changes.

Language-specific requirements
- Python (package name: redwood-inference): sample snippet must show sync and async usage, dependency pin recommendations, and a small integration test.
- Node (package name: @redwood/inference): include ESM and CommonJS examples, types for TypeScript, and bundler guidance (webpack/rollup).
- Go: provide go.mod example, context-aware request patterns, and binary size guidance.
- Java: Maven/Gradle examples and a short note on thread-safety for SDK clients.

Minimal SDK Quickstart (canonical)
- Install
  - Python: pip install redwood-inference
  - Node: npm install @redwood/inference
- Authenticate (env var): export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-...
- Example (Python):
  from redwood_inference import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
  res = client.generate(model='redwood-001', prompt='Write a short product summary')
  print(res.text)

2) Quickstarts and Templates (owner: DevEx content owners)

Canonical quickstarts (each quickstart has a short README, runnable example, and a test harness):
- Text generation (single-turn)
- Chat (multi-turn context + system messages)
- Embeddings + similarity search (indexing + query flow)
- Reranking pipeline (embedding + lexical features)
- Streaming responses with reconnect/resume
- Function/Tool calling example (declarative schema + deterministic invocation)

Template repo layout (recommended)
- /quickstart/README.md (purpose, expected runtime, cost estimate)
- /quickstart/examples/* (language folders with runnable code)
- /quickstart/tests/* (end-to-end smoke tests used by CI)
- /quickstart/metrics.yml (suggested telemetry events to instrument)

3) API Examples (owner: API product + DevEx)

Design rules for examples
- Examples should be copy-paste ready, minimal, and demonstrate common real-world patterns (pagination, streaming, error handling).
- Prefer concrete requests with realistic prompts and expected response shapes.
- Annotate examples with expected latencies and token-cost guidance.

Canonical curl example (text generation)
- curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY\" \\
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\
  -d '{\"model\": \"redwood-001\", \"prompt\": \"Summarize the following product description in one paragraph:\\n\\n<product_text>\", \"max_tokens\": 120}'

Python example (streaming response)
- See SDK streaming example: shows reconnect, chunk handling, and latency metrics emission.

4) Docs Site Operating Procedures (owner: DevEx docs site team)

Publishing workflow (high level)
1. Draft in the docs repo or Confluence sandbox and add metadata (owner, reviewers, status).
2. Technical review: SDK engineer + API product. 48-hour review SLA for minor changes; 5 business days for cross-team changes.
3. Legal/Security review for any content referencing customer data, PII, or encryption keys.
4. Merge to main and publish to docs site; trigger CI (lint, linkcheck, example smoke tests).
5. Post-publish sanity check (owner runs quick smoke example).

Versioning and Release Cadence
- Docs follow semantic release cadence aligned with SDK releases: minor/patch docs updates are continuous; major changes should be gated to the corresponding SDK/API major release.
- Maintain a change-log page for user-facing breaking changes.

Ownership & Escalation
- Every page must have an owner listed in the front-matter. Owners are responsible for keeping examples runnable and updating token-cost guidance annually.
- Escalation path for example breakage: Owner -> DevEx on-call -> SDK team -> API Product.

Draft checklist (must be green before publish)
- [ ] Code examples run in CI smoke test
- [ ] Auth patterns secure (no hard-coded keys)
- [ ] Labels and tags for discoverability present
- [ ] Reviewer approvals captured
- [ ] Related pages linked

5) Top Support Issues and Canonical Fixes (owner: DevEx support + SRE)

This section enumerates repeat support issues surfaced by the support queue during 2025-2026 and the canonical mitigations we enforce across docs and SDKs. Each entry includes: symptom, root cause, canonical fix, and doc/issue references.

Issue 1: Authentication errors (401/403)
- Symptom: Users get 401 or 403 when calling APIs from CI or serverless environments.
- Root cause: Missing or rotated API keys, or environment variable not set in CI. Some orgs accidentally set REDWOOD_API_KEY in local env but not in CI secrets.
- Canonical fix:
  1. Docs: Add CI-specific examples for GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, and GCP Cloud Build showing how to store secrets.
  2. SDKs: Improve error messaging to surface helpful hint: \"missing REDWOOD_API_KEY or invalid key; check CI secrets and key scope.\"
  3. Support playbook: Steps to validate key via curl and re-issue keys if scope mismatch.
- Related runbook: confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/auth-ci-secrets-runbook (link placeholder).

Issue 2: Streaming reconnects and partial output
- Symptom: Streaming clients see dropped connections during large responses or brief network flaps.
- Root cause: Clients not implementing incremental checkpointing / not resuming streams.
- Canonical fix:
  1. Quickstart: Provide a streaming client example with resume token handling and idempotence.
  2. SDK: Expose resume token metadata in the streaming API and document best-effort buffering strategies.
  3. Docs: Add expected SLO guidance (typical streaming session < 5s for 1k tokens; recommend chunk-size limits).

Issue 3: Unexpected output regressions after model upgrade
- Symptom: Customers report changes in generated content after model variant upgrades.
- Root cause: Model rollouts without documented prompt/eval baselines.
- Canonical fix:
  1. Release process: Mandatory pre-rollout eval set and acceptance criteria documented in the model onboarding checklist.
  2. Docs: Add migration notes and suggested prompt adjustments with small examples.
  3. Support: Offer a rollback playbook and guidance to pin a model version.

Issue 4: Embedding drift and similarity inconsistency
- Symptom: Previously similar items no longer match after embedding model change.
- Root cause: Model index mismatch; indexes built with previous embedding model.
- Canonical fix:
  1. Docs: Provide an embedding migration guide with sample re-index script and cost estimate.
  2. Template: Add an index versioning field to the stored vectors (e.g., metadata: embedding_model: redwood-embed-001).

Operational KPIs for docs maintenance
- Example smoke tests passing rate: 99.5% (target)
- Time-to-first-fix for broken examples (owner-response SLA): 48 hours (business days)
- Annual review coverage: 100% of API examples and quickstarts reviewed at least once per 12 months.

Appendices
A. Example issue triage flow (numbered steps)
1. Support ticket triaged; label with \"docs-fix\" if example broken.
2. DevEx on-call reproduces the issue and files a docs PR with failing test.
3. Owner reviews and merges; on-call verifies fix in production examples.
4. Close ticket and add postmortem note if > 4 hours to resolve.

B. Useful command snippets
- Run example smoke tests locally:
  # from repo root
  tox -e quickstarts-smoke -- examples/text-generation/python/test_smoke.py

- Validate links and front-matter:
  npm run docs:lint && npm run docs:linkcheck

C. FAQ (two high-priority items)
Q: My example works locally but fails in CI. What do I check first?
A: Verify secrets in CI, python/node version matrix, and network egress rules (corporate VPC may block external API calls).

Q: How do I request a docs page ownership change?
A: Open a PR on the docs repo that updates the front-matter owner field and add the requested owner as reviewer. For Confluence-owned pages, raise an internal request to devex-ops@redwood.ai.

Contact & Ownership
